open_points.subject: FlowEdge endpoint identity
open_points.text: a flow input or flow output endpoint has the empty string as its node (A05 rule 2), never the `flow_id`; ... `node_id`: unique within the version
open_points.question: May a FlowNode have the empty string as its `node_id`, which would make its edge endpoints indistinguishable from flow-level endpoints, or is the empty string reserved exclusively for flow endpoints?
options: Reserve the empty string for flow endpoints and refuse it as a FlowNode `node_id`.
Allow an empty FlowNode `node_id` and add another fact that distinguishes node endpoints from flow endpoints.
open_points.default_guess: Reserve the empty string for flow endpoints and refuse it as a FlowNode `node_id`.

open_points.subject: guard skipping with constants
open_points.text: A node one of whose input ports has every incoming edge disabled by its guard, or coming from a skipped node, is not executed and is recorded `skipped_by_guard` ... A typed literal pinned in a flow version and delivered to one input port like any other value
open_points.question: When an input port has no delivering edge but does have a FlowConstant, does that constant satisfy the port, or does the edge-only test still make the node `skipped_by_guard`?
options: Count constants as deliveries, so a constant-supplied port does not cause `skipped_by_guard`.
Apply the rule only to edges, so the node is `skipped_by_guard` despite the constant.
Forbid constants and edges from targeting the same input port and separately define the status of a constant-only port.
open_points.default_guess: Count constants as deliveries, so a constant-supplied port does not cause `skipped_by_guard`.

open_points.subject: NodeExecution status under mixed unavailable inputs
open_points.text: A node one of whose input ports has every incoming edge disabled by its guard, or coming from a skipped node, is not executed and is recorded `skipped_by_guard` ... a node that was not executed because its guards disabled it or an upstream node failed ... `skipped_by_guard` or `upstream_failed`
open_points.question: What status is recorded when one required input port satisfies the new `skipped_by_guard` condition while another required input is unavailable because an upstream node failed?
options: Record a different status or more than one cause.

open_points.subject: StoredValue creation during flow composition
open_points.text: `value`: the `value_id` of a StoredValue (M21) ... written when the version is composed, whose class the composing agent declares with the constant
open_points.question: Does the compose request provide literal content, schema and class for the kernel to create or reuse a StoredValue and derive its `value_id`, or does it provide an existing `value_id`; and if an existing id is allowed, how is the separately declared class reconciled with the class already encoded in that id?
options: The request supplies literal content, schema and class; the kernel creates or reuses the StoredValue and derives the id.
The request supplies only an existing `value_id`; its stored schema and class are authoritative.
Allow both literal creation and references to existing StoredValues, with explicit consistency rules.
open_points.default_guess: The request supplies literal content, schema and class; the kernel creates or reuses the StoredValue and derives the id.
